newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-ENQVIST TAKES TITLE AS RIOS WITHDRAWS IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ENQVIST TAKES TITLE AS RIOS WITHDRAWS IN FINAL.

text.p: Sweden's rising star Thomas Enqvist clinched his first title of the season when top-seeded Marcelo Rios of Chile withdrew from the Marseille Open final with a thigh injury on Sunday.

Second seed Enqvist was leading 6-4 1-0 in the second set when Rios, who had complained about a pain in his left leg after beating the unseeded Spaniard Sergi Bruguera in Saturday's semifinal, was forced to give up.
"It is a disappointing way to win. I'd rather have played the whole match because I felt very confident since the start of the tournament," said Enqvist.

The world number 10 reached the semifinals in Zagreb but was knocked out in the fourth round of the Australian Open. Things looked up when he helped Sweden to qualify for the Davis Cup quarter-finals against South Africa a week ago and the win over Rios brought him his first title of the year.
"I had a very good week and now I am looking forward to the Antwerp tournament which starts on Monday", he said.
For Rios, the week was everything but quiet. The world number seven lost his luggage at Marseille airport and then had some of his personal effects stolen from the stadium's changing rooms.
"I had a hard week. It started with all these luggage problems and finally I got injured. I could not do anything but withdraw in the final," he said.
In spite of the injury, Rios said he would go to the upcoming Antwerp tournament where he should face Adrian Voinea of Romania on Wednesday.
"I will ask for an extra day to rest and have some medical tests," he said.
